You may ONLY use statements from the given claim list and must cite every statement with its claim_id in square brackets, e.g. [C-T-A5-involutions]. Claims with level 'proved_lean' may be called machine-checked. Use 'Theorem' only for the combination stated in C-thm1.

Style: concise ML-theory preprint (6-8 pages), sober, no marketing. Sections:
Abstract (<= 180 words): the question (why do architectures fail at state tracking; circuit complexity says TC0 vs NC1), our answer for one-layer linear RNNs with Householder-product transitions (DeltaNet, DeltaProduct): an exact law h*, the first lower bound on Householder factors per token, the headline instances (A5 with involution inputs needs one reflection; A5 needs two; the S4/A5 formats of the closest prior work need two), the atlas, the preregistered training grid and its outcome, and that every statement is machine-verified or certified.

Report learnability failures honestly. (b) H-EX2 addendum: the prior work's own generator formats, Table 4 and Figure 3; state precisely what it supports and what not (it tests a sufficiency prediction against a necessity claim of prior work under our protocol and readout).

# How Many Householders Does State Tracking Need? An Exact Law for One-Layer Linear RNNs That Circuit Complexity Does Not Predict

## Abstract

The usual explanation for failures at state tracking comes from circuit complexity. Log-precision Transformers and state-space models are confined to $\mathsf{TC}^0$ [C-lit-merrill-tc0][C-lit-illusion], while bounded-width branching programs characterise $\mathsf{NC}^1$ [C-lit-barrington]. For one-layer linear RNNs whose transitions are products of generalized Householder factors (DeltaNet, DeltaProduct), we give a finer answer. A finite-state realisation with $k$ factors per token exists if and only if $k \ge h^*(G,\Sigma)$, an invariant defined over covering groups. This equivalence is proved by hand and is not machine-checked [C-thm1]. Its lower bound rests on a machine-checked lemma and a norm-free compression lemma; the compression lemma is a hand proof [C-L4][C-L2]. Several instances follow:

- $A_5$ with involution inputs needs exactly one reflection [C-T-A5-involutions].
- $A_5$ with all letters needs two [C-T-A5-all].
- The $S_4$ and $A_5$ generator formats used in prior work both need two [C-T-S4-tn][C-T-A5-c3c5].

An atlas covering 319 groups determines $h^*$ exactly for 138 of them [C-atlas]. In a preregistered training grid, our predictor matched 42 of 52 cells, and the preregistered overall criterion was not met [C-H-accuracy][C-H-gates]. Every instance value is certified by an exact verifier, and the hand-proved steps are labelled as such [C-verifier][C-redteam].

## Introduction

**The architecture debate.** Theoretical work bounds what sequence architectures can compute. Transformers with logarithmic precision can be simulated by constant-depth threshold circuits [C-lit-merrill-tc0]. State-space models "cannot express computation outside the complexity class $\mathsf{TC}^0$" and so cannot solve permutation composition [C-lit-illusion]. Self-attention cannot model periodic finite-state languages unless depth or heads grow with the input [C-lit-hahn]. With constant-bit precision, constant-depth Transformers are confined to $\mathsf{AC}^0$ [C-lit-li-cot]. Shallow shortcut solutions to automata nevertheless exist and can be understood through Krohn–Rhodes theory and circuit complexity [C-lit-liu]. Empirically, LSTMs solve regular tasks while other networks often fail [C-lit-deletang], and SSMs solve star-free state tracking exactly [C-lit-sarrof]. On this view the dividing line is $\mathsf{TC}^0$ versus $\mathsf{NC}^1$, with Barrington's characterisation of $\mathsf{NC}^1$ in the background [C-lit-barrington].

**Constructions for linear RNNs.** Positive eigenvalues cannot solve parity. Products of identity-minus-outer-product matrices with eigenvalues in $[-1,1]$ suffice for every regular language [C-lit-grazzi]; the argument uses that every orthogonal matrix is a product of reflections (Cartan–Dieudonné) [C-lit-grazzi-cd-body]. DeltaProduct uses products of $n_h$ generalized Householder transformations, and its state-tracking capability improves as $n_h$ grows [C-lit-deltaproduct]. RWKV-7 recognises all regular languages and tracks swaps on five elements [C-lit-rwkv7][C-lit-rwkv7-swaps-body]. For single-layer diagonal SSMs, non-abelian groups are out of reach, and $k$ layers suffice exactly for groups with an abelian subnormal series of length $k$ [C-lit-shakerinava].

**The gap.** None of these results gives the minimal number of Householder factors per token for a given group and input alphabet. DeltaProduct reports, unexpectedly, that $S_4$ and $A_5$ extrapolate with $n_h = 2$ "despite the theorem suggesting 3 and 4" [C-lit-deltaproduct-body]; the authors attribute this to an isomorphism with subgroups of $\mathrm{SO}(3,\mathbb{R})$ [C-lit-deltaproduct-so3-body]. A recent representation law states that the minimal $n_h$ equals the maximal reflection length $\operatorname{rank}(I-P)$ in the representation pinned by the task format (parity 1, $S_4$ 3, $A_5$/$S_5$ 4) [C-lit-howe][C-lit-howe-law-body]. The formats are $S_4$ with a transposition and a 4-cycle, and $A_5$ with a 3-cycle and a 5-cycle [C-lit-howe-format-body].

Complex KDA (arXiv:2609.24797) rules out one-layer $S_5$ tracking with $k \le 3$ Householder factors under non-expansive transitions and finite reachability, so four is the minimum under those assumptions [C-lit-ckda-thm4-body][C-lit-ckda-four-body]. Its compression picks a word of minimal Frobenius norm [C-lit-ckda-compression-body]. It also observes that tracking does not need a faithful representation, because a many-to-one decoder may merge states [C-lit-ckda-decoder-body]. A single CKDA head tracks every finite subgroup of $\mathrm{SO}(3)$ [C-lit-ckda-so3-body]. Our Lemma L2 replaces the norm-minimal word by the minimal ideal of the transition monoid. It therefore needs no norm bound and transfers the rank bound. Complex KDA defines no invariant like $h^*$ and does not state the one-reflection realisation of $A_5$ with involution inputs [C-ckda-relation].

**Contributions.**

- **An exact law (Theorem 1, proved by hand, not machine-checked).** For every finite group $G$ and generating alphabet $\Sigma$, $h^*(G,\Sigma)$ factors per token are necessary and sufficient for finite-state one-layer realisations [C-thm1]. We did not find this law over covering groups with a fixed alphabet in prior work. The closest notion, generation in codimension $k$, concerns faithful representations and has no alphabet [C-novelty][C-lit-martino-singh-body].
- **A lower bound for all groups and alphabets.** Lemma L4 (machine-checked) shows that a letter of order at least three forces $h^* \ge 2$ even through covering groups [C-L4]. Lemma L2 (proved by hand, not machine-checked) transfers this to every finite-state realisation without a norm assumption [C-L2]. That a real reflection has order two is classical [C-novelty].
- **Certified instances.** We show $h^*(A_5,\text{involutions}) = 1$, $h^*(A_5,\text{all}) = 2$, and $h^* = 2$ for both generator formats of prior work [C-T-A5-involutions][C-T-A5-all][C-T-S4-tn][C-T-A5-c3c5]. We also show $h^*(S_5,\text{all}) = 4$; this result builds on Complex KDA and includes a hand step [C-S5].
- **An atlas.** It covers all 319 groups of order at most 63 and shows that $h$ is not monotone in solvability [C-atlas][C-atlas-monotone].
- **Preregistered training experiments.** The predictor is tested against circuit-complexity and representation-law baselines, and the failures are reported [C-H-protocol][C-H-accuracy][C-X-protocol].
- **An agentic lab** with an exact verifier and a red team [C-lab][C-redteam].

## Setting and definitions

All definitions are stated in full in the companion ledger [C-ledger].

**Word problem.** A finite group $G$ is generated by an alphabet $\Sigma$. The word problem of $(G,\Sigma)$ asks for the group element represented by every prefix of an input word over $\Sigma$, for every length [C-thm1][C-L2].

**One-layer realisation.** A one-layer real recurrence has the form $h_t = A(s_t)h_{t-1} + B(s_t)$, with an arbitrary readout [C-L2]. A realisation is *finite-state* if only finitely many states are reachable [C-L2]. The transition depends only on the current token; there is no short convolution [C-thm1].

**Transition families.** A generalized Householder factor is $I - \beta u u^\top$. The family hh$k$ uses products of $k$ such factors per token [C-L1]. In our experiments $\beta \in [0,2]$ [C-H-protocol]. Exact realisations need $\beta = 2$ with unit keys; when the initial state is zero, as in DeltaNet, the input term $v = -c\,k$ supplies the offset [C-L3]. We also consider three diagonal families [C-L5][C-T-Z2-all]:

- diag_pos: real entries in $[0,1]$;
- diag_pm: real entries in $[-1,1]$;
- cdiag: complex entries of modulus at most one.

**The invariants.** $h^*(G,\Sigma)$ is the least $k$ for which the following exist:

- a finite group $H$;
- a surjection $\pi: H \to G$;
- generating lifts $t_s$ of the letters;
- a faithful real representation $\rho$ of $H$ with $\operatorname{rank}(\rho(t_s)-I) \le k$ for every letter.

$h(G,\Sigma)$ is the same minimum restricted to $H = G$ [C-thm1]. Requiring the lifts to generate $H$ does not change $h^*$ [C-thm1].

## Results I: theory

**Lemma L1 (machine-checked).** Suppose $R_1,\dots,R_k$ have rank at most one. Then $\operatorname{rank}(\prod_i (I+R_i) - I) \le k$. In particular, a token transition built from $k$ generalized Householder factors differs from the identity by rank at most $k$ [C-L1].

This is checked in Lean 4 with Mathlib. As a negative control, the strengthened bound $k-1$ is refuted in Lean. All theorems use only the standard axioms [C-L1].

**Lemma L4 (machine-checked).** A real matrix of finite order with $\operatorname{rank}(M - I) \le 1$ is an involution. Hence, take a faithful real representation $\rho$ of a finite group $H$ and a homomorphism $\pi: H\to G$ with $\pi(t) = s$, where $s$ has order at least three. Then $\operatorname{rank}(\rho(t)-I) > 1$. Consequently $h^*(G,\Sigma) \ge 2$ whenever $\Sigma$ contains a letter of order at least three, even if a larger covering group is used [C-L4].

**Lemma L2 (compression lemma; proved by hand, not machine-checked).** Suppose a one-layer real recurrence with arbitrary readout solves the word problem of $(G,\Sigma)$ for every length, with finitely many reachable states. Suppose also that $\operatorname{rank}(A(s)-I) \le k$ for every letter. Then $h^*(G,\Sigma) \le k$ [C-L2].

*Proof idea.* The reachable states form a finite transformation monoid that maps onto $G$. An idempotent $e$ of its minimal ideal gives a group $eTe$ that maps onto $G$. The compressed maps $A(u)A(s)$, restricted to the column space of the affine span of $e(Q)$, form a faithful representation of a covering group. Its generators satisfy $\operatorname{rank}(A(u)(A(s)-I)) \le k$ [C-L2].

The lemma was reviewed by two independent red-team agents. The second checked the construction exactly on adversarial instances and found it valid after wording fixes. The checked scope is: real states, affine input terms, $\beta \in [0,2]$ including singular transitions, matrix-valued states, and arbitrary readouts [C-L2].

**Lemma L3 (sufficiency; proved by hand, re-verified on every concrete instance).** Suppose $H$ maps onto $G$, with generating lifts $t_s$ and a faithful real representation $\rho$ satisfying $\operatorname{rank}(\rho(t_s)-I)\le k$. Then an exact finite-state one-layer realisation with $k$ reflections per token, using $\beta \in \{0,2\}$, exists in dimension $\dim\rho$ [C-L3]. The construction has four steps:

1. An $H$-invariant inner product makes $\rho$ orthogonal.
2. Cartan–Dieudonné factors each $\rho(t_s)$ into $\operatorname{rank}(\rho(t_s)-I)$ reflections.
3. A generic initial state separates the elements of $H$.
4. The readout maps $\rho(x)h_0$ to $\pi(x)$ [C-L3].

**Theorem 1 (proved by hand, not machine-checked; proof in the companion ledger).** For every finite group $G$ and generating alphabet $\Sigma$, a finite-state one-layer realisation of the word problem with $k$ Householder factors per token exists if and only if $k \ge h^*(G,\Sigma)$ [C-thm1][C-ledger]. Necessity is Lemma L2 and sufficiency is Lemma L3 [C-thm1]. The hypotheses are:

- real states;
- finitely many reachable states;
- token-local transitions;
- one layer;
- $\beta$ allowed to equal two [C-thm1].

**What is proved how.** Lemmas L1 and L4 are machine-checked, and their Lean sources are in the repository [C-L1][C-L4][C-ledger]. Lemmas L2 and L3 and Theorem 1 are hand proofs written out in the ledger [C-ledger]. Every certified instance lower bound therefore combines the Lean-checked Lemma L4 with the hand-proved Lemma L2 [C-T-Z3-all]. Every upper bound is an exact certificate checked by the verifier [C-T-A5-all][C-verifier].

**Computing $h$ (L6).** The codimension of the fixed space is
$\operatorname{codim}\operatorname{Fix}\rho(g) = \dim\rho - \tfrac{1}{|g|}\sum_j \chi_\rho(g^j)$.
Codimensions add over direct sums, and a sum of real irreducible representations is faithful if and only if their kernels intersect trivially. So $h(G,\Sigma)$ is a finite optimisation over the real character table [C-L6]. In general, $h^*$ can be strictly smaller than $h$, because a covering group may serve as a cheaper realisation [C-T-A5-involutions].

**Diagonal families (Lemma L5; proved by hand via the compression lemma, not machine-checked).** For finite-state one-layer realisations with closed parameter sets [C-L5]:

- diagonal transitions with entries in $[0,1]$ realise only the trivial group;
- real diagonal transitions with entries in $[-1,1]$ realise exactly the elementary abelian 2-groups;
- complex diagonal transitions realise exactly the abelian groups.

This is consistent with prior theorems on diagonal SSMs [C-L5][C-lit-shakerinava][C-lit-grazzi].

**Abelian groups (Lemma L7; proved by hand, instances certified).** For a nontrivial abelian group, $h^*(G,\Sigma)$ is one if every letter is an involution and two otherwise [C-L7]. The upper bound tracks each letter's count modulo its order (the count cover). The count cover uses dimension equal to the number of involution letters plus twice the number of other letters. This is an upper bound on the dimension, not the minimum [C-L7].

# How Many Householders Does State Tracking Need? An Exact Law for One-Layer Linear RNNs That Circuit Complexity Does Not Predict

## Abstract

The usual explanation for failures at state tracking comes from circuit complexity. Log-precision Transformers and state-space models are confined to $\mathsf{TC}^0$ [C-lit-merrill-tc0][C-lit-illusion], while bounded-width branching programs characterise $\mathsf{NC}^1$ [C-lit-barrington]. For one-layer linear RNNs whose transitions are products of generalized Householder factors (DeltaNet, DeltaProduct), we give a finer answer. A finite-state realisation with $k$ factors per token exists if and only if $k \ge h^*(G,\Sigma)$, an invariant defined over covering groups. This equivalence is proved by hand and is not machine-checked [C-thm1]. Its lower bound rests on a machine-checked lemma and a norm-free compression lemma; the compression lemma is a hand proof [C-L4][C-L2]. Several instances follow:

- $A_5$ with involution inputs needs exactly one reflection [C-T-A5-involutions].
- $A_5$ with all letters needs two [C-T-A5-all].
- The $S_4$ and $A_5$ generator formats used in prior work both need two [C-T-S4-tn][C-T-A5-c3c5].

An atlas covering 319 groups determines $h^*$ exactly for 138 of them [C-atlas]. In a preregistered training grid, our predictor matched 42 of 52 cells, and the preregistered overall criterion was not met [C-H-accuracy][C-H-gates]. Every instance value is certified by an exact verifier, and the hand-proved steps are labelled as such [C-verifier][C-redteam].

## Introduction

**The architecture debate.** Theoretical work bounds what sequence architectures can compute. Transformers with logarithmic precision can be simulated by constant-depth threshold circuits [C-lit-merrill-tc0]. State-space models "cannot express computation outside the complexity class $\mathsf{TC}^0$" and so cannot solve permutation composition [C-lit-illusion]. Self-attention cannot model periodic finite-state languages unless depth or heads grow with the input [C-lit-hahn]. With constant-bit precision, constant-depth Transformers are confined to $\mathsf{AC}^0$ [C-lit-li-cot]. Shallow shortcut solutions to automata nevertheless exist and can be understood through Krohn–Rhodes theory and circuit complexity [C-lit-liu]. Empirically, LSTMs solve regular tasks while other networks often fail [C-lit-deletang], and SSMs solve star-free state tracking exactly [C-lit-sarrof]. On this view the dividing line is $\mathsf{TC}^0$ versus $\mathsf{NC}^1$, with Barrington's characterisation of $\mathsf{NC}^1$ in the background [C-lit-barrington].

**Constructions for linear RNNs.** Positive eigenvalues cannot solve parity. Products of identity-minus-outer-product matrices with eigenvalues in $[-1,1]$ suffice for every regular language [C-lit-grazzi]; the argument uses that every orthogonal matrix is a product of reflections (Cartan–Dieudonné) [C-lit-grazzi-cd-body]. DeltaProduct uses products of $n_h$ generalized Householder transformations, and its state-tracking capability improves as $n_h$ grows [C-lit-deltaproduct]. RWKV-7 recognises all regular languages and tracks swaps on five elements [C-lit-rwkv7][C-lit-rwkv7-swaps-body]. For single-layer diagonal SSMs, non-abelian groups are out of reach, and $k$ layers suffice exactly for groups with an abelian subnormal series of length $k$ [C-lit-shakerinava].

**The gap.** None of these results gives the minimal number of Householder factors per token for a given group and input alphabet. DeltaProduct reports, unexpectedly, that $S_4$ and $A_5$ extrapolate with $n_h = 2$ "despite the theorem suggesting 3 and 4" [C-lit-deltaproduct-body]; the authors attribute this to an isomorphism with subgroups of $\mathrm{SO}(3,\mathbb{R})$ [C-lit-deltaproduct-so3-body]. A recent representation law states that the minimal $n_h$ equals the maximal reflection length $\operatorname{rank}(I-P)$ in the representation pinned by the task format (parity 1, $S_4$ 3, $A_5$/$S_5$ 4) [C-lit-howe][C-lit-howe-law-body]. The formats are $S_4$ with a transposition and a 4-cycle, and $A_5$ with a 3-cycle and a 5-cycle [C-lit-howe-format-body].

Complex KDA (arXiv:2609.24797) rules out one-layer $S_5$ tracking with $k \le 3$ Householder factors under non-expansive transitions and finite reachability, so four is the minimum under those assumptions [C-lit-ckda-thm4-body][C-lit-ckda-four-body]. Its compression picks a word of minimal Frobenius norm [C-lit-ckda-compression-body]. It also observes that tracking does not need a faithful representation, because a many-to-one decoder may merge states [C-lit-ckda-decoder-body]. A single CKDA head tracks every finite subgroup of $\mathrm{SO}(3)$ [C-lit-ckda-so3-body]. Our Lemma L2 replaces the norm-minimal word by the minimal ideal of the transition monoid. It therefore needs no norm bound and transfers the rank bound. Complex KDA defines no invariant like $h^*$ and does not state the one-reflection realisation of $A_5$ with involution inputs [C-ckda-relation].

**Contributions.**

- **An exact law (Theorem 1, proved by hand, not machine-checked).** For every finite group $G$ and generating alphabet $\Sigma$, $h^*(G,\Sigma)$ factors per token are necessary and sufficient for finite-state one-layer realisations [C-thm1]. We did not find this law over covering groups with a fixed alphabet in prior work. The closest notion, generation in codimension $k$, concerns faithful representations and has no alphabet [C-novelty][C-lit-martino-singh-body].
- **A lower bound for all groups and alphabets.** Lemma L4 (machine-checked) shows that a letter of order at least three forces $h^* \ge 2$ even through covering groups [C-L4]. Lemma L2 (proved by hand, not machine-checked) transfers this to every finite-state realisation without a norm assumption [C-L2]. That a real reflection has order two is classical [C-novelty].
- **Certified instances.** We show $h^*(A_5,\text{involutions}) = 1$, $h^*(A_5,\text{all}) = 2$, and $h^* = 2$ for both generator formats of prior work [C-T-A5-involutions][C-T-A5-all][C-T-S4-tn][C-T-A5-c3c5]. We also show $h^*(S_5,\text{all}) = 4$; this result builds on Complex KDA and includes a hand step [C-S5].
- **An atlas.** It covers all 319 groups of order at most 63 and shows that $h$ is not monotone in solvability [C-atlas][C-atlas-monotone].
- **Preregistered training experiments.** The predictor is tested against circuit-complexity and representation-law baselines, and the failures are reported [C-H-protocol][C-H-accuracy][C-X-protocol].
- **An agentic lab** with an exact verifier and a red team [C-lab][C-redteam].

## Setting and definitions

All definitions are stated in full in the companion ledger [C-ledger].

**Word problem.** A finite group $G$ is generated by an alphabet $\Sigma$. The word problem of $(G,\Sigma)$ asks for the group element represented by every prefix of an input word over $\Sigma$, for every length [C-thm1][C-L2].

**One-layer realisation.** A one-layer real recurrence has the form $h_t = A(s_t)h_{t-1} + B(s_t)$, with an arbitrary readout [C-L2]. A realisation is *finite-state* if only finitely many states are reachable [C-L2]. The transition depends only on the current token; there is no short convolution [C-thm1].

**Transition families.** A generalized Householder factor is $I - \beta u u^\top$. The family hh$k$ uses products of $k$ such factors per token [C-L1]. In our experiments $\beta \in [0,2]$ [C-H-protocol]. Exact realisations need $\beta = 2$ with unit keys; when the initial state is zero, as in DeltaNet, the input term $v = -c\,k$ supplies the offset [C-L3]. We also consider three diagonal families [C-L5][C-T-Z2-all]:

- diag_pos: real entries in $[0,1]$;
- diag_pm: real entries in $[-1,1]$;
- cdiag: complex entries of modulus at most one.

**The invariants.** $h^*(G,\Sigma)$ is the least $k$ for which the following exist:

- a finite group $H$;
- a surjection $\pi: H \to G$;
- generating lifts $t_s$ of the letters;
- a faithful real representation $\rho$ of $H$ with $\operatorname{rank}(\rho(t_s)-I) \le k$ for every letter.

$h(G,\Sigma)$ is the same minimum restricted to $H = G$ [C-thm1]. Requiring the lifts to generate $H$ does not change $h^*$ [C-thm1].

## Results I: theory

**Lemma L1 (machine-checked).** Suppose $R_1,\dots,R_k$ have rank at most one. Then $\operatorname{rank}(\prod_i (I+R_i) - I) \le k$. In particular, a token transition built from $k$ generalized Householder factors differs from the identity by rank at most $k$ [C-L1].

This is checked in Lean 4 with Mathlib. As a negative control, the strengthened bound $k-1$ is refuted in Lean. All theorems use only the standard axioms [C-L1].

**Lemma L4 (machine-checked).** A real matrix of finite order with $\operatorname{rank}(M - I) \le 1$ is an involution. Hence, take a faithful real representation $\rho$ of a finite group $H$ and a homomorphism $\pi: H\to G$ with $\pi(t) = s$, where $s$ has order at least three. Then $\operatorname{rank}(\rho(t)-I) > 1$. Consequently $h^*(G,\Sigma) \ge 2$ whenever $\Sigma$ contains a letter of order at least three, even if a larger covering group is used [C-L4].

**Lemma L2 (compression lemma; proved by hand, not machine-checked).** Suppose a one-layer real recurrence with arbitrary readout solves the word problem of $(G,\Sigma)$ for every length, with finitely many reachable states. Suppose also that $\operatorname{rank}(A(s)-I) \le k$ for every letter. Then $h^*(G,\Sigma) \le k$ [C-L2].

*Proof idea.* The reachable states form a finite transformation monoid that maps onto $G$. An idempotent $e$ of its minimal ideal gives a group $eTe$ that maps onto $G$. The compressed maps $A(u)A(s)$, restricted to the column space of the affine span of $e(Q)$, form a faithful representation of a covering group. Its generators satisfy $\operatorname{rank}(A(u)(A(s)-I)) \le k$ [C-L2].

The lemma was reviewed by two independent red-team agents. The second checked the construction exactly on adversarial instances and found it valid after wording fixes. The checked scope is: real states, affine input terms, $\beta \in [0,2]$ including singular transitions, matrix-valued states, and arbitrary readouts [C-L2].

**Lemma L3 (sufficiency; proved by hand, re-verified on every concrete instance).** Suppose $H$ maps onto $G$, with generating lifts $t_s$ and a faithful real representation $\rho$ satisfying $\operatorname{rank}(\rho(t_s)-I)\le k$. Then an exact finite-state one-layer realisation with $k$ reflections per token, using only $\beta = 0$ or $\beta = 2$, exists in dimension $\dim\rho$ [C-L3]. The construction has four steps:

1. An $H$-invariant inner product makes $\rho$ orthogonal.
2. Cartan–Dieudonné factors each $\rho(t_s)$ into $\operatorname{rank}(\rho(t_s)-I)$ reflections.
3. A generic initial state separates the elements of $H$.
4. The readout maps $\rho(x)h_0$ to $\pi(x)$ [C-L3].

**Theorem 1 (proved by hand, not machine-checked; proof in the companion ledger).** For every finite group $G$ and generating alphabet $\Sigma$, a finite-state one-layer realisation of the word problem with $k$ Householder factors per token exists if and only if $k \ge h^*(G,\Sigma)$ [C-thm1][C-ledger]. Necessity is Lemma L2 and sufficiency is Lemma L3 [C-thm1]. The hypotheses are:

- real states;
- finitely many reachable states;
- token-local transitions;
- one layer;
- $\beta$ allowed to equal two [C-thm1].

**What is proved how.** Lemmas L1 and L4 are machine-checked, and their Lean sources are in the repository [C-L1][C-L4][C-ledger]. Lemmas L2 and L3 and Theorem 1 are hand proofs written out in the ledger [C-ledger]. Every certified instance lower bound therefore combines the Lean-checked Lemma L4 with the hand-proved Lemma L2 [C-T-Z3-all]. Every upper bound is an exact certificate checked by the verifier [C-T-A5-all][C-verifier].

**Computing $h$ (L6).** The codimension of the fixed space is
$\operatorname{codim}\operatorname{Fix}\rho(g) = \dim\rho - \tfrac{1}{|g|}\sum_j \chi_\rho(g^j)$.
Codimensions add over direct sums, and a sum of real irreducible representations is faithful if and only if their kernels intersect trivially. So $h(G,\Sigma)$ is a finite optimisation over the real character table [C-L6]. In general, $h^*$ can be strictly smaller than $h$, because a covering group may serve as a cheaper realisation [C-T-A5-involutions].

**Diagonal families (Lemma L5; proved by hand via the compression lemma, not machine-checked).** For finite-state one-layer realisations with closed parameter sets [C-L5]:

- diagonal transitions with entries in $[0,1]$ realise only the trivial group;
- real diagonal transitions with entries in $[-1,1]$ realise exactly the elementary abelian 2-groups;
- complex diagonal transitions realise exactly the abelian groups.

This is consistent with prior theorems on diagonal SSMs [C-L5][C-lit-shakerinava][C-lit-grazzi].

**Abelian groups (Lemma L7; proved by hand, instances certified).** For a nontrivial abelian group, $h^*(G,\Sigma)$ is one if every letter is an involution and two otherwise [C-L7]. The upper bound tracks each letter's count modulo its order (the count cover). The count cover uses dimension equal to the number of involution letters plus twice the number of other letters. This is an upper bound on the dimension, not the minimum [C-L7].

The realisation is the so3 construction in dimension 3, whereas the permutation representation costs 4 [C-T-A5-all]. The same value holds for the alphabets of 3-cycles and of 5-cycles [C-T-A5-cycles3][C-T-A5-cycles5].

**The generator formats of prior work.** For $S_4$ with alphabet tn (a transposition and a 4-cycle) and $A_5$ with alphabet c3c5 (a 3-cycle and a 5-cycle), $h^* = 2$ [C-T-S4-tn][C-T-A5-c3c5][C-X-protocol]. Both are realised by the so3 construction in dimension 3. The permutation-representation costs are 3 and 4 respectively [C-T-S4-tn][C-T-A5-c3c5]. These values agree with DeltaProduct's observation that $n_h = 2$ suffices for $S_4$ and $A_5$ [C-lit-deltaproduct-body]. They are below the format-pinned values of the representation law [C-lit-howe-law-body].

**$S_5$.** The certified bounds alone give $2 \le h^*(S_5,\text{all}) \le 4$, with $h(S_5,\text{all}) = 4$ [C-T-S5-all]. Combining a hand step with a published result closes this interval to $h^*(S_5,\text{all}) = 4$ under exact finite reachability [C-S5]. The hand step goes as follows. A cover with $\operatorname{rank}(\rho(t_s)-I)\le 3$ can be made orthogonal by averaging. Rank at most 3 leaves at most one non-real eigenvalue pair, so the cover is a single-head, orthogonal, finite-state tracker of the kind excluded by arXiv:2609.24797 [C-S5][C-lit-ckda-thm4-body]. The argument only needs an alphabet containing a 5-cycle and a transposition [C-S5]. It therefore also covers the tn alphabet of $S_5$, whose certified bounds alone are 2 and 4 [C-T-S5-tn][C-lit-howe-format-body]. With transpositions only, one reflection suffices [C-T-S5-transpositions].

**Elementary abelian groups.** We have $h^*(\mathbb{Z}_2^3,\text{all}) = 1$, while $h(\mathbb{Z}_2^3,\text{all}) = 3$ [C-T-Z2p3-all]. The count cover uses a covering group of order 128 in dimension 7, and diag_pm realises the word problem exactly as well [C-T-Z2p3-all]. Likewise $h^*(\mathbb{Z}_2^2,\text{all}) = 1$ while $h(\mathbb{Z}_2^2,\text{all}) = 2$ [C-T-Z2p2-all].

**Other groups.**
- Cyclic groups of order at least three need two factors, by Lemma L4 [C-T-Z3-all][C-T-Z5-all][C-T-Z6-all].
- $S_3$, $D_4$, $D_5$ and $A_4$ with all letters need two [C-T-S3-all][C-T-D4-all][C-T-D5-all][C-T-A4-all].
- Symmetric groups with transposition alphabets need one [C-T-S3-transpositions][C-T-S4-transpositions][C-T-S5-transpositions].
- For $Q_8$ the interval remains open: $2 \le h^*(Q_8,\text{all}) \le 6$, with $h(Q_8,\text{all}) = 4$ [C-T-Q8-all].

**Diagonal families on these instances.**
- diag_pos realises none of the instances [C-T-Z2-all][C-T-A5-all].
- diag_pm realises $\mathbb{Z}_2$, $\mathbb{Z}_2^2$ and $\mathbb{Z}_2^3$ but not $\mathbb{Z}_3$ [C-T-Z2-all][C-T-Z2p2-all][C-T-Z2p3-all][C-T-Z3-all].
- cdiag realises the cyclic and elementary abelian instances but no non-abelian one [C-T-Z5-all][C-T-S3-transpositions].

**Contrast with circuit complexity.** The solvable–non-solvable boundary does not order these values:

- The non-solvable $A_5$ with all letters costs the same two factors as the solvable $S_3$, $S_4$ and $A_4$ [C-T-A5-all][C-T-S3-all][C-T-S4-all][C-T-A4-all].
- $A_5$ with involution inputs costs one factor, less than the abelian $\mathbb{Z}_3$ [C-T-A5-involutions][C-T-Z3-all].
- The non-solvable $S_5$ with transpositions costs one factor [C-T-S5-transpositions].

## Results III: the atlas

**Coverage and agreement.** The atlas covers all 319 groups of order at most 63 in the GAP SmallGroups library, with the full alphabet [C-atlas]. Our numerical character tables and GAP's exact tables give the same faithful $h$ for every group, with 0 disagreements [C-atlas]. $h^*$ is determined exactly for 138 of the 319 groups: 32 of 213 non-abelian groups, and every abelian group by Lemma L7 [C-atlas]. The only non-solvable group in the atlas is $A_5$, with $h = 2$ and $h^* = 2$ [C-atlas-nonsolvable]. Figure 2 and Table 3 show the atlas.

**Non-monotonicity.** Of the 212 solvable non-abelian groups, 181 have faithful $h \ge 3$ [C-atlas-monotone]. Every faithful representation of these groups needs more Householder factors per token than the non-solvable $A_5$ [C-atlas-monotone]. The largest faithful $h$ in the atlas is 10, attained by C11:C5 [C-atlas-monotone].

For $h^*$, these groups have only certified bounds of the form $[2,\text{upper}]$. A strict separation in $h^*$ is therefore not claimed [C-atlas-monotone].

**Distribution of $h$ over non-abelian groups.** Listed as value of faithful $h$ followed by the number of groups, the distribution is 2: 32, 3: 8, 4: 115, 5: 11, 6: 41, 8: 5, 10: 1 [C-atlas-dist].

**Sign lifts.** Multiplying a letter's matrix by $-1$ gives a lift to $G\times\mathbb{Z}_2$ [C-atlas-twist]. These sign lifts lower the certified upper bound below the faithful $h$ for 37 of the 213 non-abelian groups [C-atlas-twist].

## Results IV: preregistered experiments

### H-EX1: the training grid

**Protocol.** The protocol was committed before the first confirmatory run [C-H-protocol]:

- **Models:** one-layer diag_pos, diag_pm, hh1, hh2, hh3, hh4 (DeltaNet/DeltaProduct with $\beta\in[0,2]$) and an LSTM [C-H-protocol].
- **Architecture:** 64-dimensional state, MLP readout [C-H-protocol].
- **Seeds:** 20 seeds (1000–1019) per cell [C-H-protocol].
- **Training:** 3000 steps, with a length curriculum from 8 to 64 and a final stage at 128 [C-H-protocol].
- **Seed success:** token accuracy at least 0.9 on positions 257–512 of length-512 sequences [C-H-protocol].
- **Cell success:** at least 10 of 20 seeds succeed [C-H-protocol].
- **Grid:** 9 tasks × 7 architectures [C-H-protocol].

This parameterisation reaches $\beta = 0$ and $\beta = 2$ exactly, which exact realisability requires [C-open-beta].

**Predictors.** Our algebraic predictor derives each cell's expected outcome from the certified values of Table 1 and from Lemma L5. Where the certified interval does not decide a cell, the prediction is left undetermined, as for hh2 and hh3 on $S_5$/all [C-G-hh2-S5-all][C-G-hh3-S5-all]. The baselines are [C-H-accuracy]:

- circuit class (solvable or not);
- abelian or not;
- group size;
- the representation law in the permutation representation;
- faithful representations only.

**Cell outcomes.** Figure 1 and Table 2 show all cells. Several outcomes match the theory:

- hh1 succeeds on $S_3$/transpositions and $S_5$/transpositions with 20 of 20 seeds [C-G-hh1-S3-transpositions][C-G-hh1-S5-transpositions].
- hh1 fails on $S_3$/all (0 of 20), while hh2 succeeds (19 of 20) [C-G-hh1-S3-all][C-G-hh2-S3-all].
- diag_pm succeeds on $\mathbb{Z}_2^3$/all (20 of 20) and fails on $\mathbb{Z}_3$/all (0 of 20) [C-G-diag_pm-Z2p3-all][C-G-diag_pm-Z3-all].
- On $A_5$/involutions, hh3 and hh4 succeed with 20 of 20 seeds [C-G-hh3-A5-involutions][C-G-hh4-A5-involutions].

**Learnability failures.** Several cells that are exactly realisable failed in training:

- On $A_5$/involutions, hh1 and hh2 reached 0 of 20 seeds, both at chance-level mean accuracy 0.017 [C-G-hh1-A5-involutions][C-G-hh2-A5-involutions].
- On $A_5$/all, every Householder width failed with 0 of 20 seeds, including hh2, hh3 and hh4 [C-G-hh2-A5-all][C-G-hh3-A5-all][C-G-hh4-A5-all].
- hh1 on $\mathbb{Z}_2^3$/all reached 1 of 20 [C-G-hh1-Z2p3-all].
- hh2 on $\mathbb{Z}_2$/all reached 3 of 20 [C-G-hh2-Z2-all].
- hh4 on $\mathbb{Z}_2$/all reached 6 of 20 [C-G-hh4-Z2-all].
- hh3 on $\mathbb{Z}_3$/all reached 6 of 20 [C-G-hh3-Z3-all].

In several of these cells the in-distribution accuracy is high while extrapolation fails, for example hh4 on $\mathbb{Z}_2$/all with in-distribution mean accuracy 1.000 [C-G-hh4-Z2-all].

**Device sensitivity.** Because of a runner bug, the same protocol and seeds ran on both the MPS GPU and the CPU [C-H-replication]:

- hh1 on $\mathbb{Z}_2$/all: 18 of 20 on MPS, 0 of 20 on CPU [C-H-replication].
- diag_pos on $\mathbb{Z}_2$/all: 0 of 20 on both [C-H-replication].

Training outcomes can therefore depend strongly on floating-point details of the device [C-H-replication].

**Predictor accuracy.** Agreement with the cell outcomes on the determined cells [C-H-accuracy]:

| Predictor | Agreement |
|---|---|
| Representation law, permutation representation | 45 of 52 [C-H-accuracy] |
| Faithful representations only | 43 of 52 [C-H-accuracy] |

**What H-EX2 supports and what it does not.** H-EX2 tests a sufficiency prediction, $h^* = 2$, against a necessity claim of prior work, under our protocol and readout [C-X-protocol][C-lit-howe-law-body].

What it supports: on $A_5$/c3c5, two factors per token suffice for length generalisation under our protocol, which agrees with DeltaProduct's observation [C-X-hh2-A5-c3c5][C-lit-deltaproduct-body].

What it does not support:
- The $S_4$/tn cell with two factors failed, so the sufficiency prediction was not borne out there [C-X-hh2-S4-tn].
- It does not refute the representation law in the setting where that law was stated, which pins a representation through the task format and restricts how the input acts [C-lit-howe][C-lit-howe-law-body].
- Learnability under a given optimiser is not implied by the existence of an exact realisation (Theorem 1). Several H-EX1 cells show this gap directly [C-thm1][C-G-hh2-A5-all].

## The agentic lab and the verification pipeline

**Lab structure.** The results were produced in an agentic lab [C-lab] with these components:

- a literature scout whose quotes are checked by code;
- an integrator;
- a cascade of four researcher agents;
- an exact verifier;
- a red-team agent;
- a preregistration for each round.

The lab ran 15 rounds at a cost of 10.51 USD [C-lab]. Nine rounds produced an accepted claim, and all nine survive re-checking with the hardened verifier, with 0 withdrawn [C-lab]. Six rounds produced a negative result [C-lab]. The scout kept 60 literature findings whose verbatim quote was found by code in the abstract [C-lab]. Every literature claim in this paper was title-checked against arXiv or Crossref, and every quote was checked by code [C-lit-deltaproduct-body][C-lit-barrington].

**Verifier.** The domain verifier passed its mandatory self-test of 46 known true and known false claims [C-verifier]. The test set includes near-boundary cases, such as the same matrices without the sign lift and $k$ one below the certified value, as well as regressions for every red-team bug [C-verifier].

**Accepted rounds.** Accepted rounds include a certified $h^*(A_5,\text{all}) = 2$ (round 5) and the lower bound $h^*(S_4,\text{all}) \ge 2$ (round 7) [C-expressivity-R5][C-expressivity-R7]. Rounds 4, 6 and 8 are marked as contested by a red-team counter-check [C-expressivity-R4][C-expressivity-R6][C-expressivity-R8].

**Agent interpretations are not results.** Several attached interpretations are inconsistent with the hardened consistency rule. In round 3 the agent's interpretation that $h^*(A_5,\text{involutions})$ exceeds one is contradicted by the certified value one [C-expressivity-R3-I][C-T-A5-involutions]. The round 2 interpretation is likewise flagged [C-expressivity-R2-I].

**Negative rounds.** In six rounds no claim passed the verifier and the consistency rule [C-neg1][C-neg2][C-neg3][C-neg4][C-neg5][C-neg6]:

- F3: one reflection for $A_5$ with involution inputs.
- F25: $k$ of 2 or 3 for $S_5$ via a non-permutational representation.
- F26: a pattern for $S_n$.
- F13: an exact lower bound for $A_5$/involutions via covers.
- F21: $S_4$ with involutions.
- F11: $\mathbb{Z}_2^3$ under sign twists.

**Loophole closed.** In round 1 an agent answered "no" to the one-reflection question for $A_5$ with involutions and backed the answer with two true but weaker checks. The verifier had refuted the agent's claim $h^* = 2$ by finding a $k = 1$ certificate [C-loophole1]. The consistency rule now requires an impossibility certificate for negative answers and exact-value checks for numbers [C-loophole1].

**Red team.** An independent read-and-execute red-team agent found three bugs [C-redteam]:

1. The group names S1, D1 and D2 denoted wrong groups.
2. The published $h^*$ sentence omitted the finite-state hypothesis.
3. The consistency rule accepted unchecked numbers.

All three were fixed and turned into regression cases [C-redteam]. The red team confirmed the exact core: 189 library constructions and 15556 exhaustive explicit-matrix claims against an independent re-implementation, and the character tables of all 319 SmallGroups against GAP, gave 0 disagreements [C-redteam]. A separate theory red team contributed the open-parameterisation corollary and the complex-state remark [C-open-beta][C-complex].

## Limitations and open questions

**Hypotheses of the law.** Theorem 1 assumes finitely many reachable states, real states, token-local transitions without short convolution, one layer, and $\beta$ allowed to equal two [C-thm1].

**Hand proofs.** The compression lemma, the theorem, Lemmas L5 and L7, and the $S_5$ lower bound are hand proofs, not machine-checked [C-L2][C-thm1][C-L5][C-L7][C-S5]. Only Lemmas L1 and L4 are machine-checked [C-L1][C-L4].

**Complex states.** A complex realisation of complex rank $k$ only gives $h^* \le 2k$. For example, a $1\times 1$ complex rotation tracks $\mathbb{Z}_3$ with complex rank one, while $h^*(\mathbb{Z}_3,\text{all}) = 2$ [C-complex].

**Exact versus floating-point arithmetic.**
- If $\beta$ is confined to $[0, 2)$, as with a sigmoid parameterisation, no nontrivial group is exactly realisable for any number of factors [C-open-beta]. The same holds for open intervals of diagonal entries. Trained models with such parameterisations can only approximate, and the theory's predictions for them concern approximation (corollary proved by hand) [C-open-beta].
- Floating-point details of the training device changed one cell from 18 of 20 to 0 of 20 [C-H-replication].

**Open intervals.**
- $Q_8$ remains between 2 and 6 [C-T-Q8-all].
- In the atlas, $h^*$ is determined exactly for only 138 of 319 groups [C-atlas].
- Most solvable non-abelian groups carry only bounds of the form $[2,\text{upper}]$ [C-atlas-monotone].

**Multiple layers.** For diagonal SSMs, depth interacts with subnormal series [C-lit-shakerinava]. A multi-layer analogue of $h^*$ is open.

**Chain of thought and padding.** Intermediate generation increases Transformer expressivity, by an amount that depends on its length [C-lit-cot][C-lit-li-cot]. Whether extra tokens can act as an additional Householder budget per input symbol is a hypothesis we have not tested [C-lit-cot].

**Learnability.** The grid shows that exact realisability does not imply learnability under our protocol. The clearest cases are $A_5$ with all letters, where no width learned [C-G-hh4-A5-all], and $A_5$ with involutions, where one and two factors did not learn [C-G-hh1-A5-involutions][C-G-hh2-A5-involutions].
